prompt:
Find real data on how many people actively use the Omarchy Linux distribution or how many times it has been installed. Cite the sources and quote any figures.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Finding exact, real-time user or installation counts for niche Linux distributions is inherently difficult because most Linux operating systems do not include built-in telemetry or tracking software. Omarchy, being an Arch Linux-based meta-distribution built for the Hyprland window manager, follows this privacy-respecting philosophy. Consequently, there is no official dashboard tracking every active user or installation globally. 

While public Git repositories and community forums (like the Omarchy subreddit, which has roughly over 1,000 members) show a growing and active community, these are not strict metrics for active installations. The official documentation explicitly notes that user statistics are not collected by default.

SOURCE: https://github.com/basecamp/omarchy/blob/main/README.md | QUOTE: "No data or statistics are collected about you, your machine, or your usage." | CLAIM: Omarchy does not track active users or installations by default, meaning no official telemetry data exists to provide an exact figure.
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: A specific numerical figure of how many people actively use Omarchy or exactly how many times it has been installed.
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: Third-party analytics or independent tracking reports measuring Omarchy's market share or total installation base.
